item: A read that fails on a damaged page of an encrypted file no longer leaves its pooled connection poisoned
summary: On an encrypted library (SQLCipher) a read of a page that fails its check left that connection answering an empty MemoryError to every later page read, healthy tables included, until it was closed (measured; rollback, commit, shrink_memory and a second key do not clear it, and a plain SQLite connection is not affected). A pooled connection went back in that state, so one request that touched a damaged page left a connection that failed every later request with the text of a real out-of-memory until the process restarted. The damage observer (damage.discard_poisoned_connection, called from the handle_error listener attach registers) now marks that one connection as a disconnect and keeps the rest of the pool (invalidate_pool_on_disconnect off); the pool opens a fresh connection on the next checkout and the error the caller sees is unchanged. It discards on a SQLCipher code 11 and on an empty MemoryError raised on a SQLCipher connection, because the last overflow page of a long value fails silently (the read returns the right length with wrong tail bytes, measured, and the poison arrives on the next statement); it never latches or records on a MemoryError, which names no file. A wrong key (code 26), a plain SQLite file's corruption, a MemoryError with a message and a closed or absent connection are never reclassified. A statement run on the driver's own cursor over a pooled connection raises past the observer, so the country-code scan, the incremental vacuum and the WAL checkpoint go through one helper, damage.guard_raw_driver, which discards the connection and names the file. A session on a discarded connection loses what it had flushed and must roll back before it commits. tests/test_poisoned_connection.py runs on real encrypted stores, including the canaries that the poison is still there without the observer and without the guard.
